title: WATCH: Phoenix musician composes Hindi song dedicated to Jacob and Duduzane Zuma

 WATCH: Phoenix musician composes Hindi song dedicated to Jacob and Duduzane Zuma
 Neesha Maharaj | Published 2 days ago Copy to Clipboard Ask AI Shirley Singh who uses the stage name Jenny Maharaj. 
 Image: Supplied
 A Phoenix musician and former MK Party candidate says she wrote a Hindi song praising Jacob Zuma and his son, Duduzane, after being approached by the party.
 Shirley Singh who uses the stage name Jenny Maharaj, composed the song ‘Hum Khaan Ka Rishta Hai’ which translates to ‘We Are Related by Blood’, after she was approached by the party to write a song for them in Hindi.
 Singh, 64, said she was approached by Cebo, a musician who was the MK Party’s resident singer to write a song in Hindi, which illustrated that the party cared for the Indian community.
 “The Hindi lyrics I wrote was fused with Cebo’s Zulu lyrics. I was shocked at the request because I had one day to come up with a song. I turned down the offer initially because of the short notice. However, Cebo convinced me to write the song because he loved my voice,” said Singh.
 Singing for 58 years, Singh had performed with numerous bands, including the Concords, Revolvers and Suhana Sungeet.
 Initially, Singh had approached musician Rajive Mohan, who died two weeks ago, to help her with the lyrics.
 However, he was busy and Singh had written her own song within a few hours.
 Her song recognised the struggles of her community which had to deal with water cuts, infrastructure damage, poverty and hunger.
 She also sings of the MK Party making a difference in her community.
 For the past six years Singh took an interest in helping the communities of Phoenix and Verulam handle service delivery issues, assisting the indigent and the elderly.
 “Over the years I saw the struggles of my people. In 2024 I joined the MK Party so I could be empowered to help the communities of Phoenix and Verulam,” said Singh.
 Singh, who did not win in the recent elections said she ‘idolised’ Jacob Zuma because he showed a lot of affection and helped the Indian community in Phoenix when he was president.
 “I believe Duduzane Zuma is a great leader. During my interaction with him as a candidate councillor I found him to be respectful, warm and humble. I pray that he is president one day. I see him as a great future leader,” she added.
